transcript.text: Based on my therapy assessments, the South unit patient failed the sit-to-stand assessment and requires a full-body bariatric lift for every bed-to-chair transfer. The North unit patient can currently complete a two-person stand-pivot transfer with a gait belt. From a clinical standpoint, the South unit patient has a clear and immediate need for the bariatric lift, while the North unit patient has a viable alternative transfer method available.

transcript.text: From a facilities standpoint, I need to flag an important physical constraint. The available lift is the Titan-MB model, which has a 48-inch turning radius. This fits South room 412's 50-inch doorway, but North room 318 has a 36-inch doorway and cannot safely accommodate this lift. Additionally, the charger must be placed in the South 4B equipment alcove. So from a facilities perspective, the lift can only be safely deployed to the South unit.

transcript.text: From a nursing education standpoint, I can confirm that three South-unit nurses have completed the lift competency validation. Hospital policy requires two validated staff members for every lift transfer, and South's available coverage with validated staff is 07:00 to 19:00 daily. So South can meet the staffing requirement for safe lift operations during those hours.

transcript.text: From an infection prevention standpoint, I need to flag that the South unit patient is on contact precautions. Because of this, the lift plan requires a dedicated extra-large sling labeled specifically for South room 412, and a documented disinfecting wipe-down of the lift must be performed after each transfer. These infection control measures need to be built into the operational plan before the lift assignment is finalized.
